subject.title: [Bug]: sandbox-browser noVNC clipboard garbles non-Latin-1 characters (CJK, Cyrillic, etc.)

question: Should OpenClaw replace the sandbox-browser VNC server stack to support UTF-8 Extended Clipboard, and which security-preserving implementation should be sponsored?
rationale: The bug is source-supported, but the obvious TigerVNC direction changes the display/VNC server boundary and the earlier candidate PR showed concrete auth and binding pitfalls.

options.title: Sponsor secured TigerVNC replacement
options.body: Replace x11vnc/Xvfb with a VNC server that supports Extended Clipboard while preserving VncAuth, localhost-only raw VNC exposure, token bootstrap, Docker image contracts, and live noVNC paste proof.

options.title: Add browser text insertion instead
options.body: Keep the current noVNC stack and solve non-Latin input through a separate browser/CDP insertion action, accepting that the noVNC clipboard panel remains limited.

options.title: Document known limitation
options.body: Leave x11vnc in place and document the noVNC UTF-8 clipboard limitation until a sandbox-browser owner chooses a secure VNC-stack direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor secured TigerVNC replacement
recommendation.body: Replace x11vnc/Xvfb with a VNC server that supports Extended Clipboard while preserving VncAuth, localhost-only raw VNC exposure, token bootstrap, Docker image contracts, and live noVNC paste proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for both sandbox-browser introduction and noVNC auth hardening points to steipete.
